suggestions.quote: The turn breaks "A number can't lie to you": it didn't lie, it described the crowd and you were never the crowd.
suggestions.fix: Keep the cue intent steady through the city montage and change it on or after the spoken turn line, not on the first shot of the lit-up city. The cue before that line should still read as the 'number is truth' intent.

suggestions.quote: his chip falls to zero the moment he nods
suggestions.fix: Hold the music's intent change until the nod and the chip reaching zero (the split-flap lands on 0). Cut to a wordless HOLD of about 2 s with the cousin's face (sad) and the hall sound dropping out. No cue shift on the line that sets up the nod.

suggestions.quote: Your own, in the phone camera: 0.04%.
suggestions.fix: A phone-camera view is hard to stage side-on. Stage it as an over-the-shoulder insert: your head large in the foreground, the phone screen as a paper rectangle with a mirror of you and the chip, and your shocked face reaction within 2 s of the number.

suggestions.quote: The whole city lit up, almost every chip small, and one sourced long shot that worked among them
suggestions.fix: Build the city as three drifting skyline layers with tiny chips as dots (no new rigged figures) and a slow camera pull-back. Show the long shot as one figure whose chip is brighter, so it does not need a new set. This is the main build risk in the draft, so cut the long shot at G2 if the source is not found.

suggestions.quote: The teacher's chance of finishing the syllabus: three per cent. The loud boy: zero. The topper's real dream is music: nought point two. The chaiwala's café: sixty-one.
suggestions.fix: Give each reveal a separate camera move or pose change, because four chips in a row would stall. The numbers should be split-flap counters on the scene, not narrated figures in a row, and each reveal gets a face reaction. Use the chaiwala's sixty-one as the beat that triggers your switch to a safe target.

suggestions.quote: Your younger cousin at the nets, his chip at nought point two
suggestions.fix: Reuse: the hall and its chip rig are shared with the city. The nets or lane is the only extra set, and the same lane serves the last beat (the bat thwack). Draw it as a flat side-on strip with one stump prop, a bat, and a drifting fence layer. Reuse the pause-time kit's kid (cap) figure, with the cousin's bubble limited to something like 'Okay, bhaiya.'

suggestions.quote: Your cousin's bat thwacks in the lane outside.
suggestions.fix: Show it as sound plus a bat leaning in the doorway, off faces, with nothing on the right third of the frame in the last 15 s. The end-card tags go left and the chip is not drawn. This is a sound-only payoff of the plant at line 37 (the bat behind the cupboard).

Continuity of the rule device: say in the script which figures keep a glowing chip and that your chip is the only crimson one, with the thumbnail's crimson chip matching the film. Keep the stranger (crimson head) hidden somewhere in the hall with no chip, so crimson does not read as 'danger' twice.
